title: Restricting level Hom bijections to compatible systems
statement: Let C,C′,J,J′,B,τ,F,σ,uInv,I,P,V,a be the coefficient towers, actual sequence-site systems, ordinary inverse-image system, and level adjunctions of [lem-coef-ordinary-inverse-system] and [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Let K be an OrdinaryDirectSystemCore as in [lem-coef-ordinary-direct-system-core], including its local mate condition for two arbitrary component maps. Then there is an equivalence (P.pull M → N) ≃ (M → K.push N) for all systems M,N, whose nth component, followed by K.component_n.hom, is a_n.homEquiv applied to P.component_n.inv followed by evaluation_n of the original morphism. No finite-limit, set-adjunction, or geometric construction hypothesis is needed to prove this local-to-global assertion once K is supplied.

proof.text: A compatible family of component module-sheaf maps assembles into a map on the actual sequence site: use the nth map at (n,U). Every product-site arrow factors as a vertical arrow and a horizontal arrow; vertical naturality and the given horizontal squares prove naturality. Linearity is transported across the evaluation coefficient identity. Evaluation recovers the original family, and component evaluations jointly detect equality. The private helpers systemHom_naturality, systemHomApp, systemHomMk and systemHomMk_evaluation prove these statements explicitly.

At each level form the equivalence obtained by precomposing with P.component_n.inv, applying the level adjunction, then postcomposing with K.component_n.inv. The core local mate condition transports horizontal compatibility in both directions. Assemble the resulting families with systemHomMk. The level equivalences have inverse laws, and joint faithfulness of evaluations proves the two global inverse laws. Evaluation of the constructed forward map and cancellation of the core component isomorphism give homEquiv_component.

statement_change.what: The original core identified vertical components but imposed no condition on horizontal transitions. Over a constant nonzero ring, identity inverse image and the functor retaining components but zeroing every nonidentity transition satisfy the old core. The promised transpose of the identity of a constant nonzero system would have identity components into that zero-transition system, which is not a system morphism. Add the local two-component mate law to the geometric core, and prove the global restriction of Hom equivalences from that law; the main existence theorem and OrdinaryDirectSystem are unchanged.
